title: Universal entropic occupation statistics in disordered bosonic resonators
abstract: Programmable microcavities support grand-canonical photon gases. We show that bosonic state counting creates an entropic staircase of most-probable total occupations. For detuning density continuous and nonzero at the chemical-potential threshold, the active-cell fraction is asymptotically linear at low temperature and the conditional law has a universal limit; for uniform disorder the law is exact over a finite temperature interval. For two modes it is the Gauss--Kuzmin distribution, linking photonic thermodynamics and metric number theory. We outline finite-array and dye-microcavity tests.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the occupation statistics in arrays of disordered bosonic resonators coupled to a thermal reservoir. It derives an entropic staircase governing the most probable total occupations and establishes that for two modes, the low-temperature limit follows the Gauss–Kuzmin distribution. This links photonic thermodynamics directly to fundamental concepts in number theory.
main_problem: The paper investigates the universal occupation statistics arising when multiple bosonic resonators sample a distribution of chemical-potential offsets (detunings) from a common reservoir.
main_result: For two modes, the low-temperature limit yields the Gauss–Kuzmin distribution, linking photonic thermodynamics to metric number theory. Furthermore, for uniform disorder, this law remains exact up to a finite temperature $T^*$.
method: The analysis involves minimizing an entropic potential $\phi_k(x)$ derived from bosonic state counting and analyzing conditional probability ratios in the grand-canonical ensemble.
model_or_system: The system consists of programmable microcavities supporting bosonic resonators, modeled as multiple independent cells coupled to a large reservoir at fixed temperature $T$ and chemical potential $\mu$. The key variable is the detuning $\epsilon_i = E_i - \mu$.
key_observables: Most-probable total occupations ($K(x)$), conditional occupation probabilities ($p^{(q)}_k$), and the active cell fraction $A(T)$.
important_parameters: Temperature $T$, chemical potential $\mu$, detuning density $ho(\epsilon)$, and the dimensionless variable $x =  eta\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the grand-canonical ensemble description, assuming that finite-reservoir effects are negligible for small total occupations.

paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the entropic staircase via potential minimization. It then derives the conditional law for two modes, identifying the Gauss–Kuzmin distribution in the low-temperature limit and analyzing its exactness under uniform disorder.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep connection between bosonic statistics (photonic systems) and number theory (Gauss–Kuzmin), offering universal statistical laws applicable to disordered quantum optical systems.

Below the horizontal axis, the straight lines are ϕk = kx −ln(k + 1), with x = βϵ and k = 0, . . . , 10; black dots mark successive crossings of the lower envelope. Above the axis, the same abscissa carries the staircase K(x). The ordinate is split: it denotes K above zero and ϕk = βΦk below zero. The K = 0 plateau lies on the horizontal axis for x > ln 2.

FIG. 2. Temperature and disorder dependence of the dominant occupation number. (Left) Conditional active-cell distributions on a logarithmic scale. The reference distribution is p(2) k , obtained exactly for uniform disorder at every 0 < τ ≤1 and shown in blue. The red and purple points show the probability distributions for a representative nonuniform detuning density ρ(ϵ) = (1 + 4ϵ/∆)/(3∆) at temperatures τ = 1 and τ = 1/4, respectively, approaching p(2) k as T →0. (Right) Dominant- occupation-number sector map for a uniform detuning band, in u = ϵ/∆and τ = T/T∗.
